````math
## Appendix C Relation to Concurrent Work

##### Overlapping results with Hsu and Xu.

In concurrent work, [Hsu and Xu \[2026\]](#bib.bib25) prove that an
$`H`$-head attention layer with a degree-$`D`$ polynomial-threshold
readout representing $`f`$ must satisfy $`DH\geq\deg_{\pm}(f)`$, and
that this lower bound is exact for symmetric functions. At $`D=1`$,
their result agrees with our symmetric characterization in
Theorem [5](#Thmtheorem5 "Theorem 5 (Exact symmetric characterization). ‣ 2.2 Exact Head Complexity for Symmetric Functions ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"),
giving the same minimum head count for nonconstant symmetric functions.
We developed the symmetric characterization independently of the
publicly released Hsu–Xu manuscript.

##### Differences from Hsu and Xu.

Their model omits positional embeddings, whereas our fixed-query,
linear-readout model allows arbitrary additive positional embeddings
shared across heads.
Theorem [5](#Thmtheorem5 "Theorem 5 (Exact symmetric characterization). ‣ 2.2 Exact Head Complexity for Symmetric Functions ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention")
therefore shows that positional information does not lower the required
head count for symmetric functions. Beyond the symmetric setting, we
additionally derive an exact linear-fractional normal form, prove the
universal bound $`H^{\ast}(f)\leq 2^{n}-1`$, and exhibit a nonsymmetric
function with $`\deg_{\pm}(f)=2<3\leq H^{\ast}(f)`$, showing that
threshold degree does not characterize head complexity. Additionally, we
also make publicly available a Lean 4 formalization of the attention
model and the main results, including the symmetric characterization,
the linear-fractional normal form, and the nonsymmetric separation.

##### Head complexity bounds of Rajaraman et al.

[Rajaraman et al. \[2026\]](#bib.bib26) prove that $`n`$-bit parity
needs exactly $`n`$ heads, agreeing with
Corollary [2](#Thmcorollary2 "Corollary 2 (Parity). ‣ 2.2 Exact Head Complexity for Symmetric Functions ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention").
Their lower bounds permit arbitrary embeddings of token-position pairs,
while their constructions use additive embeddings. Their Lemma 8 also
obtains a polynomial sign representation of degree at most the head
count by clearing positive denominators, matching the implication of our
Theorem [2](#Thmtheorem2 "Theorem 2 (Threshold-degree lower bound). ‣ Unnormalized attention weights (denominator). ‣ 2.1.1 Why the correspondence holds ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention")
in a more general embedding model. They further establish a $`2^{n}`$
universal upper bound, an $`\Omega(2^{n}/n^{2})`$ lower bound for almost
all Boolean functions, and dimension and precision compactness bounds.

## Appendix D Model Details

This section gives a self-contained specification of the model
underlying
Equations ([1](#S2.E1 "In Setup ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"))
and ([2](#S2.E2 "In Setup ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention")).
Fix an input length $`n`$ and a number of heads $`H`$. The model
receives an $`n`$-bit input, applies a single multi-head self-attention
update, and classifies the resulting representation at a dedicated query
position.
Figure [1](#S2.F1 "Figure 1 ‣ Setup ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention")
gives an overview of this computation.

##### Input sequence and representations.

For $`\mathbf{x}=(x_{1},\ldots,x_{n})\in\{0,1\}^{n}`$, append a
dedicated query token $`q`$ to form the sequence
$`(x_{1},\ldots,x_{n},q)`$. The query token is a distinguished
vocabulary element, for which the symbol $`=`$ is one possible choice.
Let $`\mathcal{I}:=[n]\cup\{q\}`$ denote the set of sequence positions.

Choose a model dimension $`d_{\mathrm{model}}`$, token embeddings
$`\mathbf{e}_{0},\mathbf{e}_{1},\mathbf{e}_{q}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\mathrm{model}}}`$,
and positional embeddings
$`\mathbf{p}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{p}_{n},\mathbf{p}_{q}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\mathrm{model}}}`$.
Following the standard additive positional-encoding convention, the
representation at each position is the sum of its token embedding and
its positional embedding:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbf{u}_{j}(\mathbf{x})=\begin{cases}\mathbf{e}_{x_{j}}+\mathbf{p}_{j},&j\in[n],\\
\mathbf{e}_{q}+\mathbf{p}_{q},&j=q.\end{cases}
``` |  | (8) |

In each case, the first term identifies the token occupying the position
and the second encodes the position itself. Since the token at the query
position is always $`q`$, $`\mathbf{u}_{q}`$ is independent of
$`\mathbf{x}`$. These token and positional embeddings are shared across
heads; each head operates on the same embedded sequence
$`\{\mathbf{u}_{j}(\mathbf{x})\}_{j\in\mathcal{I}}`$.

##### Single-head attention update.

Choose a head dimension $`d_{\mathrm{head}}`$. Each head $`h\in[H]`$ has
its own query, key, and value projections

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
W_{Q}^{(h)},W_{K}^{(h)},W_{V}^{(h)}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\mathrm{head}}\times d_{\mathrm{model}}}
``` |  | (9) |

and output projection
$`W_{O}^{(h)}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\mathrm{model}}\times d_{\mathrm{head}}}`$.
At the query position, head $`h`$ assigns position $`j\in\mathcal{I}`$
the logit and normalized attention weight

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle\ell_{j}^{(h)}(\mathbf{x})`$ | $`\displaystyle=\left\langle W_{K}^{(h)}\mathbf{u}_{j}(\mathbf{x}),W_{Q}^{(h)}\mathbf{u}_{q}\right\rangle,`$ |  | (10) |
|  | $`\displaystyle a_{j}^{(h)}(\mathbf{x})`$ | $`\displaystyle=\frac{\exp\!\left(\ell_{j}^{(h)}(\mathbf{x})\right)}{\sum_{r\in\mathcal{I}}\exp\!\left(\ell_{r}^{(h)}(\mathbf{x})\right)}.`$ |  | (11) |

Its contribution to the query position is

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbf{y}_{q}^{(h)}(\mathbf{x})=W_{O}^{(h)}\sum_{j\in\mathcal{I}}a_{j}^{(h)}(\mathbf{x})W_{V}^{(h)}\mathbf{u}_{j}(\mathbf{x})\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\mathrm{model}}}.
``` |  | (12) |

Only the output at $`q`$ is used for readout; outputs at other positions
are not analyzed in this work.

##### Multi-head output and readout.

The projected head outputs are added to the residual stream at the query
position:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbf{h}_{q}(\mathbf{x})=\mathbf{u}_{q}+\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbf{y}_{q}^{(h)}(\mathbf{x}).
``` |  | (13) |

Given a readout vector $`\mathbf{w}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\mathrm{model}}}`$
and threshold $`\tau\in\mathbb{R}`$, an $`H`$-head configuration exactly
represents $`f:\{0,1\}^{n}\to\{0,1\}`$ if

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\forall\mathbf{x}\in\{0,1\}^{n},\qquad\bigl[f(\mathbf{x})=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\left\langle\mathbf{w},\mathbf{h}_{q}(\mathbf{x})\right\rangle>\tau\bigr].
``` |  | (14) |

The head complexity $`H^{\ast}(f)`$ is the minimum
$`H\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}`$ over all choices of dimensions, embeddings,
projections, and readout parameters that exactly represent $`f`$.

##### Conventions and scope.

All parameters are real-valued, and $`d_{\mathrm{model}}`$ and
$`d_{\mathrm{head}}`$ are unrestricted. The usual factor
$`1/\sqrt{d_{\mathrm{head}}}`$ in scaled dot-product attention is
omitted because it can be absorbed into the query or key projections.
Likewise, $`W_{O}^{(h)}`$ can be composed with $`W_{V}^{(h)}`$; we
retain the output projections to distinguish the model and head
dimensions. The residual $`\mathbf{u}_{q}`$ is independent of
$`\mathbf{x}`$ and can therefore be absorbed into the readout threshold.
Unrestricted width allows the shared embeddings to allocate orthogonal
coordinate blocks selected by different heads.

The query token occurs last, so full attention and a standard causal
mask expose it to the same set of positions. The architecture contains
no MLP, layer normalization, dropout, or additional layers.

## Appendix E Proofs of the Main Results

### E.1 Linear-Fractional Normal Form

We prove that the admissibility conditions in
Definition [1](#Thmdefinition1 "Definition 1 (Linear-fractional atom). ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention")
characterize exactly the coefficients obtained from the one-head
parameterization. We then establish both directions of the scalar-score
representation in
Theorem [1](#Thmtheorem1 "Theorem 1 (Linear-fractional normal form). ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"),
including simultaneous realization of all atoms with shared embeddings.

##### Parameterization and affine coefficients.

For $`\gamma,\alpha,\rho_{1},\ldots,\rho_{n}>0`$ and
$`\eta,\beta,m_{1},\ldots,m_{n}\in\mathbb{R}`$, define

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\phi(\mathbf{x})=\frac{\eta+\sum_{i=1}^{n}\rho_{i}\alpha^{x_{i}}(m_{i}+\beta x_{i})}{\gamma+\sum_{i=1}^{n}\rho_{i}\alpha^{x_{i}}},\qquad\mathbf{x}\in\{0,1\}^{n}.
``` |  | (15) |

For Boolean inputs, $`\alpha^{x_{i}}=1+(\alpha-1)x_{i}`$ and
$`x_{i}^{2}=x_{i}`$. Expanding the numerator and denominator therefore
gives
Equation ([4](#S2.E4 "In Definition 1 (Linear-fractional atom). ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention")),
with

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle A_{i}`$ | $`\displaystyle=\rho_{i}\bigl((\alpha-1)m_{i}+\alpha\beta\bigr),`$ | $`\displaystyle b`$ | $`\displaystyle=\eta+\sum_{i}\rho_{i}m_{i},`$ |  | (16) |
|  | $`\displaystyle C_{i}`$ | $`\displaystyle=\rho_{i}(\alpha-1),`$ | $`\displaystyle d`$ | $`\displaystyle=\gamma+\sum_{i}\rho_{i}.`$ |  |  |

##### Exact coefficient constraints.

A tuple $`(\mathbf{A},b,\mathbf{C},d)`$ is obtained from
Equation ([16](#A5.E16 "In Parameterization and affine coefficients. ‣ E.1 Linear-Fractional Normal Form ‣ Appendix E Proofs of the Main Results ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"))
if and only if it is admissible in the sense of
Definition [1](#Thmdefinition1 "Definition 1 (Linear-fractional atom). ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention").
We prove necessity directly from the coefficient formulas, then give
explicit parameters for every admissible tuple.

Condition (i) of
Definition [1](#Thmdefinition1 "Definition 1 (Linear-fractional atom). ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention")
is equivalent to $`d+\sum_{i}\min\{0,C_{i}\}>0`$. Under condition (ii),
it therefore reduces to $`d>0`$ when the denominator slopes are positive
or all zero, and to $`d+\sum_{i}C_{i}>0`$ when they are negative. A
mixture of zero and nonzero denominator slopes is excluded.

##### Necessity.

The denominator in
Equation ([15](#A5.E15 "In Parameterization and affine coefficients. ‣ E.1 Linear-Fractional Normal Form ‣ Appendix E Proofs of the Main Results ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"))
is strictly positive on the Boolean cube. Since
$`C_{i}=\rho_{i}(\alpha-1)`$ and every $`\rho_{i}>0`$, its slopes have a
common strict sign when $`\alpha\neq 1`$. When $`\alpha=1`$, all
$`C_{i}=0`$ and $`A_{i}=\rho_{i}\beta`$, giving the stated restriction
on the numerator slopes. The case $`n=0`$ has no slopes and only
requires $`d>0`$.

##### Sufficiency.

Fix an admissible tuple. Evaluating its denominator at
$`\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}`$ gives $`d>0`$. If
$`\mathbf{C}\neq\mathbf{0}`$, set $`S=\sum_{i}|C_{i}|`$ and choose

|     |                                                        |     |      |
|-----|--------------------------------------------------------|-----|------|
|     |
       ``` math
       \alpha=\begin{cases}2+S/d,&C_{i}>0\text{ for all }i,\\
       (d-S)/(2d),&C_{i}<0\text{ for all }i.\end{cases}
       ```                                                     |     | (17) |

In the negative case, denominator positivity at
$`\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{1}`$ gives $`S<d`$. In both cases, $`\alpha>0`$,
and the assignments

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle\rho_{i}`$ | $`\displaystyle=\frac{C_{i}}{\alpha-1},`$ | $`\displaystyle\gamma`$ | $`\displaystyle=d-\sum_{i}\rho_{i},`$ |  | (18) |
|  | $`\displaystyle\beta`$ | $`\displaystyle=0,`$ | $`\displaystyle m_{i}`$ | $`\displaystyle=\frac{A_{i}}{C_{i}},\qquad\eta=b-\sum_{i}\rho_{i}m_{i}`$ |  |  |

have $`\rho_{i}>0`$ and $`\sum_{i}\rho_{i}<d`$, hence $`\gamma>0`$.
Substitution into
Equation ([16](#A5.E16 "In Parameterization and affine coefficients. ‣ E.1 Linear-Fractional Normal Form ‣ Appendix E Proofs of the Main Results ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"))
recovers the prescribed tuple exactly.

If $`\mathbf{C}=\mathbf{0}`$ and $`\mathbf{A}\neq\mathbf{0}`$, let
$`\sigma\in\{-1,1\}`$ be the common sign of the $`A_{i}`$ and put
$`q=1+\sum_{i}|A_{i}|/d`$. Set

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\alpha=1,\quad\beta=\sigma q,\quad\rho_{i}=|A_{i}|/q,\quad\gamma=d-\sum_{i}\rho_{i},\quad m_{i}=0,\quad\eta=b.
``` |  | (19) |

Then $`\rho_{i}>0`$, $`\gamma>0`$, and $`\rho_{i}\beta=A_{i}`$. If
$`\mathbf{A}=\mathbf{C}=\mathbf{0}`$, take $`\alpha=1`$,
$`\beta=m_{i}=0`$, $`\eta=b`$, and $`\rho_{i}=\gamma=d/(n+1)`$. This
also covers $`n=0`$. Thus every admissible coefficient tuple comes from
the parameterization.

##### Coefficient representations.

Admissibility concerns the chosen coefficients. A function is an atom
whenever it has *some* admissible representation, even if another
representation of the same function fails the conditions. For example,
on $`\{0,1\}^{2}`$,

|     |                                                  |     |
|-----|--------------------------------------------------|-----|
|     |
       ``` math
       x_{1}-x_{2}=\frac{2x_{1}-2x_{2}}{1+x_{1}+x_{2}}.
       ```                                               |     |

The constant-denominator representation on the left has mixed numerator
slopes and fails condition (iii) of
Definition [1](#Thmdefinition1 "Definition 1 (Linear-fractional atom). ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"),
while the representation on the right is admissible. This identity, like
the affine expansion of each head, uses the Boolean-input assumption.

##### Decomposing the readout score.

Fix an $`H`$-head model with readout $`(\mathbf{w},\tau)`$, and let
$`\mathbf{y}_{q}^{(h)}(\mathbf{x})`$ denote the projected output of head
$`h`$, that is, the $`h`$-th summand in
Equation ([1](#S2.E1 "In Setup ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention")).
Define its scalar contribution after readout by

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
g^{(h)}(\mathbf{x}):=\left\langle\mathbf{w},\mathbf{y}_{q}^{(h)}(\mathbf{x})\right\rangle,\qquad h\in[H],
``` |  | (20) |

Taking the inner product of
Equation ([1](#S2.E1 "In Setup ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"))
with $`\mathbf{w}`$ then gives

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\left\langle\mathbf{w},\mathbf{h}_{q}(\mathbf{x})\right\rangle=\left\langle\mathbf{w},\mathbf{u}_{q}\right\rangle+\sum_{h=1}^{H}g^{(h)}(\mathbf{x}),
``` |  | (21) |

Subtracting the threshold $`\tau`$ gives the input-independent constant
$`c=\langle\mathbf{w},\mathbf{u}_{q}\rangle-\tau`$ in
Equation ([5](#S2.E5 "In Theorem 1 (Linear-fractional normal form). ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention")).
Thus, the forward direction of
Theorem [1](#Thmtheorem1 "Theorem 1 (Linear-fractional normal form). ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention")
reduces to showing that each $`g^{(h)}`$ is a linear-fractional atom.

##### From a head to an atom.

For a head $`h`$, define

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbf{q}^{(h)}=W_{Q}^{(h)}\mathbf{u}_{q},\qquad\Delta\mathbf{e}=\mathbf{e}_{1}-\mathbf{e}_{0}.
``` |  | (22) |

The query vector $`\mathbf{q}^{(h)}`$ is independent of the input. Since
$`x_{i}\in\{0,1\}`$, the representation at input position $`i`$ can be
written as

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbf{u}_{i}(\mathbf{x})=\mathbf{e}_{x_{i}}+\mathbf{p}_{i}=\mathbf{e}_{0}+\mathbf{p}_{i}+x_{i}\Delta\mathbf{e}.
``` |  | (23) |

Let $`\ell_{j}^{(h)}(\mathbf{x})`$ denote the attention logit at
position $`j`$, and let $`s_{j}^{(h)}(\mathbf{x})`$ denote its scalar
value after the value projection, output projection, and readout:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\ell_{j}^{(h)}(\mathbf{x})=\left\langle W_{K}^{(h)}\mathbf{u}_{j}(\mathbf{x}),\mathbf{q}^{(h)}\right\rangle,\qquad s_{j}^{(h)}(\mathbf{x})=\left\langle\mathbf{w},W_{O}^{(h)}W_{V}^{(h)}\mathbf{u}_{j}(\mathbf{x})\right\rangle.
``` |  | (24) |

Substituting
Equation ([23](#A5.E23 "In From a head to an atom. ‣ E.1 Linear-Fractional Normal Form ‣ Appendix E Proofs of the Main Results ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"))
into the logit gives

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle\ell_{i}^{(h)}(\mathbf{x})`$ | $`\displaystyle=\left\langle W_{K}^{(h)}(\mathbf{e}_{0}+\mathbf{p}_{i}),\mathbf{q}^{(h)}\right\rangle+x_{i}\left\langle W_{K}^{(h)}\Delta\mathbf{e},\mathbf{q}^{(h)}\right\rangle,`$ |  | (25) |
|  | $`\displaystyle\exp\!\left(\ell_{i}^{(h)}(\mathbf{x})\right)`$ | $`\displaystyle=\rho_{i}^{(h)}\bigl(\alpha^{(h)}\bigr)^{x_{i}},`$ |  | (26) |

where

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\rho_{i}^{(h)}=\exp\!\left(\left\langle W_{K}^{(h)}(\mathbf{e}_{0}+\mathbf{p}_{i}),\mathbf{q}^{(h)}\right\rangle\right),\qquad\alpha^{(h)}=\exp\!\left(\left\langle W_{K}^{(h)}\Delta\mathbf{e},\mathbf{q}^{(h)}\right\rangle\right).
``` |  | (27) |

Likewise, substituting
Equation ([23](#A5.E23 "In From a head to an atom. ‣ E.1 Linear-Fractional Normal Form ‣ Appendix E Proofs of the Main Results ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"))
into the scalar value gives

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle s_{i}^{(h)}(\mathbf{x})`$ | $`\displaystyle=m_{i}^{(h)}+\beta^{(h)}x_{i},`$ |  | (28) |
|  | $`\displaystyle m_{i}^{(h)}`$ | $`\displaystyle=\left\langle\mathbf{w},W_{O}^{(h)}W_{V}^{(h)}(\mathbf{e}_{0}+\mathbf{p}_{i})\right\rangle,\qquad\beta^{(h)}=\left\langle\mathbf{w},W_{O}^{(h)}W_{V}^{(h)}\Delta\mathbf{e}\right\rangle.`$ |  | (29) |

Thus $`\rho_{i}^{(h)}`$ and $`m_{i}^{(h)}`$ are the unnormalized
attention weight and the value of position $`i`$ when $`x_{i}=0`$, while
$`\alpha^{(h)}`$ is the factor gained and $`\beta^{(h)}`$ the shift
incurred when $`x_{i}=1`$. The latter two depend only on
$`\Delta\mathbf{e}`$, so they are the same at every position. At the
query position, both quantities are input-independent. Set

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\gamma^{(h)}=\exp\!\left(\left\langle W_{K}^{(h)}\mathbf{u}_{q},\mathbf{q}^{(h)}\right\rangle\right),\qquad\eta^{(h)}=\gamma^{(h)}\left\langle\mathbf{w},W_{O}^{(h)}W_{V}^{(h)}\mathbf{u}_{q}\right\rangle.
``` |  | (30) |

The scalar contribution of head $`h`$ to the readout score is therefore

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle g^{(h)}(\mathbf{x})`$ | $`\displaystyle=\frac{\sum_{j\in\mathcal{I}}\exp\!\left(\ell_{j}^{(h)}(\mathbf{x})\right)s_{j}^{(h)}(\mathbf{x})}{\sum_{j\in\mathcal{I}}\exp\!\left(\ell_{j}^{(h)}(\mathbf{x})\right)}`$ |  |  |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle=\frac{\eta^{(h)}+\sum_{i=1}^{n}\rho_{i}^{(h)}\bigl(\alpha^{(h)}\bigr)^{x_{i}}\bigl(m_{i}^{(h)}+\beta^{(h)}x_{i}\bigr)}{\gamma^{(h)}+\sum_{i=1}^{n}\rho_{i}^{(h)}\bigl(\alpha^{(h)}\bigr)^{x_{i}}}.`$ |  | (31) |

The exponential definitions give
$`\rho_{i}^{(h)},\alpha^{(h)},\gamma^{(h)}>0`$, so
Equation ([31](#A5.E31 "In From a head to an atom. ‣ E.1 Linear-Fractional Normal Form ‣ Appendix E Proofs of the Main Results ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"))
has the parameterization in
Equation ([15](#A5.E15 "In Parameterization and affine coefficients. ‣ E.1 Linear-Fractional Normal Form ‣ Appendix E Proofs of the Main Results ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention")).
Applying
Equation ([16](#A5.E16 "In Parameterization and affine coefficients. ‣ E.1 Linear-Fractional Normal Form ‣ Appendix E Proofs of the Main Results ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"))
to head $`h`$ yields the affine ratio in
Equation ([4](#S2.E4 "In Definition 1 (Linear-fractional atom). ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention")),
with admissible coefficients. Hence $`g^{(h)}`$ is an atom in the sense
of
Definition [1](#Thmdefinition1 "Definition 1 (Linear-fractional atom). ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention").
By
Equation ([21](#A5.E21 "In Decomposing the readout score. ‣ E.1 Linear-Fractional Normal Form ‣ Appendix E Proofs of the Main Results ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention")),
the complete pre-threshold score is

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\left\langle\mathbf{w},\mathbf{h}_{q}(\mathbf{x})\right\rangle-\tau=\underbrace{\left\langle\mathbf{w},\mathbf{u}_{q}\right\rangle-\tau}_{c}+\sum_{h=1}^{H}g^{(h)}(\mathbf{x}).
``` |  | (32) |

Thus every $`H`$-head representation gives an $`H`$-atom representation,
proving $`L_{\mathrm{frac}}(f)\leq H^{\ast}(f)`$.

##### From atoms to heads.

Conversely, consider a score $`c+\sum_{h=1}^{H}\phi_{h}(\mathbf{x})`$
with atoms as in
Definition [1](#Thmdefinition1 "Definition 1 (Linear-fractional atom). ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention").
For each atom, choose parameters in
Equation ([15](#A5.E15 "In Parameterization and affine coefficients. ‣ E.1 Linear-Fractional Normal Form ‣ Appendix E Proofs of the Main Results ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"))
that produce its affine coefficients, and index these parameters by
$`h`$. The coefficient characterization above guarantees such a choice.
If $`H=0`$, take $`\mathbf{w}=0`$ and $`\tau=-c`$ to realize the
constant score. For $`H\geq 1`$, choose $`d_{\mathrm{model}}\geq 4H`$
and orthonormal vectors
$`\mathbf{q}^{(h)},\mathbf{k}^{(h)},\mathbf{v}^{(h)},\mathbf{o}^{(h)}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\mathrm{model}}}`$
for each $`h`$. Let $`d_{\mathrm{head}}\geq 1`$ be arbitrary, and fix a
unit vector $`\mathbf{r}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\mathrm{head}}}`$. Choose the
embeddings

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle\mathbf{e}_{0}`$ | $`\displaystyle=0,`$ | $`\displaystyle\mathbf{e}_{1}`$ | $`\displaystyle=\sum_{h}\left((\log\alpha^{(h)})\mathbf{k}^{(h)}+\beta^{(h)}\mathbf{v}^{(h)}\right),`$ |  | (33) |

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle\mathbf{e}_{q}`$ | $`\displaystyle=\sum_{h}\left(\mathbf{q}^{(h)}+(\log\gamma^{(h)})\mathbf{k}^{(h)}+\frac{\eta^{(h)}}{\gamma^{(h)}}\mathbf{v}^{(h)}\right),`$ |  | (34) |
|  | $`\displaystyle\mathbf{p}_{i}`$ | $`\displaystyle=\sum_{h}\left((\log\rho_{i}^{(h)})\mathbf{k}^{(h)}+m_{i}^{(h)}\mathbf{v}^{(h)}\right),\qquad\mathbf{p}_{q}=0.`$ |  |  |

For each head $`h`$, define the linear maps on these directions by

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
W_{Q}^{(h)}\mathbf{q}^{(h)}=\mathbf{r},\qquad W_{K}^{(h)}\mathbf{k}^{(h)}=\mathbf{r},\qquad W_{V}^{(h)}\mathbf{v}^{(h)}=\mathbf{r},\qquad W_{O}^{(h)}\mathbf{r}=\mathbf{o}^{(h)},
``` |  | (35) |

extending each map by zero on the orthogonal complement of its displayed
input direction. The logits at input position $`i`$ and the query
position are

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\log\rho_{i}^{(h)}+x_{i}\log\alpha^{(h)}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\log\gamma^{(h)},
``` |  | (36) |

and the corresponding scalar values in the $`\mathbf{o}^{(h)}`$
direction are $`m_{i}^{(h)}+\beta^{(h)}x_{i}`$ and
$`\eta^{(h)}/\gamma^{(h)}`$. Hence head $`h`$ writes
$`\phi_{h}(\mathbf{x})\mathbf{o}^{(h)}`$. Choose
$`\mathbf{w}=\sum_{h}\mathbf{o}^{(h)}`$ and $`\tau=-c`$. The query
residual is orthogonal to the readout, so the resulting scalar score is
exactly $`c+\sum_{h}\phi_{h}(\mathbf{x})`$ on every Boolean input. This
proves the reverse direction of
Equation ([5](#S2.E5 "In Theorem 1 (Linear-fractional normal form). ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention")).
Thresholding the score and minimizing over $`H`$ yields
$`H^{\ast}(f)=L_{\mathrm{frac}}(f)`$.

### E.2 One-Head Characterization

We prove
Corollary [1](#Thmcorollary1 "Corollary 1 (One head). ‣ Unnormalized attention weights (denominator). ‣ 2.1.1 Why the correspondence holds ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention").

##### Zero heads.

When $`H=0`$,
Equation ([1](#S2.E1 "In Setup ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"))
reduces to $`\mathbf{h}_{q}(\mathbf{x})=\mathbf{u}_{q}`$, which is
independent of $`\mathbf{x}`$. Every zero-head classifier is therefore
constant. Conversely, either constant function can be realized by
placing the readout threshold above or below the fixed score
$`\langle\mathbf{w},\mathbf{u}_{q}\rangle`$. Hence $`H^{\ast}(f)=0`$ if
and only if $`f`$ is constant.

##### At most one head implies linear threshold.

Suppose $`H^{\ast}(f)\leq 1`$. The zero-head case is covered above.
Otherwise,
Theorem [1](#Thmtheorem1 "Theorem 1 (Linear-fractional normal form). ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention")
gives a constant $`c`$ and one atom $`\phi=N/D`$ such that
$`f(\mathbf{x})=1`$ exactly when $`c+\phi(\mathbf{x})>0`$. The numerator
$`N`$ and denominator $`D`$ are affine on the Boolean cube, and
$`D(\mathbf{x})>0`$. Therefore

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
c+\phi(\mathbf{x})=\frac{cD(\mathbf{x})+N(\mathbf{x})}{D(\mathbf{x})}
``` |  | (37) |

has the same sign as the affine function $`cD+N`$. Thus $`f`$ is a
linear threshold function.

##### Linear threshold implies at most one head.

Suppose $`f(\mathbf{x})=1`$ exactly when
$`\theta_{0}+\sum_{i=1}^{n}\theta_{i}x_{i}>0`$. Consider

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\phi(\mathbf{x})=\frac{\theta_{0}+\sum_{i=1}^{n}\theta_{i}x_{i}}{1+\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_{i}}.
``` |  | (38) |

Its denominator is strictly positive and has all slopes equal to one.
Hence its coefficients are admissible by
Definition [1](#Thmdefinition1 "Definition 1 (Linear-fractional atom). ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"),
and it is an atom with the same sign as the given affine threshold
function. This also covers $`n=0`$, when both slope vectors are empty.
Taking $`c=0`$ in
Definition [2](#Thmdefinition2 "Definition 2 (Linear-fractional complexity). ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention")
yields $`L_{\mathrm{frac}}(f)\leq 1`$, and
Theorem [1](#Thmtheorem1 "Theorem 1 (Linear-fractional normal form). ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention")
then gives $`H^{\ast}(f)\leq 1`$.

### E.3 Threshold-Degree Lower Bound

We prove
Theorem [2](#Thmtheorem2 "Theorem 2 (Threshold-degree lower bound). ‣ Unnormalized attention weights (denominator). ‣ 2.1.1 Why the correspondence holds ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention").
Equation ([4](#S2.E4 "In Definition 1 (Linear-fractional atom). ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"))
writes each atom as a ratio of affine functions with a denominator that
is strictly positive on the Boolean cube. By
Theorem [1](#Thmtheorem1 "Theorem 1 (Linear-fractional normal form). ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"),
after moving the readout threshold into a constant, an $`H`$-head
classifier therefore has a scalar score

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
S(\mathbf{x})=c+\sum_{h=1}^{H}\frac{N_{h}(\mathbf{x})}{D_{h}(\mathbf{x})},\qquad D_{h}(\mathbf{x})>0,
``` |  | (39) |

where $`N_{h}`$ and $`D_{h}`$ are affine. Since the domain is finite,
the threshold can be perturbed so that $`S`$ is strictly positive on
inputs labelled one and strictly negative on inputs labelled zero.
Multiplication by the positive common denominator preserves this sign
pattern and gives

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
P(\mathbf{x})=c\prod_{h=1}^{H}D_{h}(\mathbf{x})+\sum_{h=1}^{H}N_{h}(\mathbf{x})\prod_{g\neq h}D_{g}(\mathbf{x}).
``` |  | (40) |

Every summand has degree at most $`H`$, so $`P`$ is a
degree-at-most-$`H`$ sign representation. Minimizing over $`H`$ proves
$`\deg_{\pm}(f)\leq H^{\ast}(f)`$.

### E.4 Strict Separation from Threshold Degree

We prove
Theorem [3](#Thmtheorem3 "Theorem 3 (Strict separation from threshold degree). ‣ Strictness of the lower bound. ‣ 2.1.1 Why the correspondence holds ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention")
for the function in
Equation ([6](#S2.E6 "In Strictness of the lower bound. ‣ 2.1.1 Why the correspondence holds ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention")).
For its Boolean blocks $`\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b}\in\{0,1\}^{5}`$,
introduce the sign coordinates

|     |                                                      |     |      |
|-----|------------------------------------------------------|-----|------|
|     |
       ``` math
       s_{i}=1-2a_{i},\qquad t_{i}=1-2b_{i},\qquad i\in[5],
       ```                                                   |     | (41) |

so $`\mathbf{s},\mathbf{t}\in\{-1,+1\}^{5}`$. Define the corresponding
quadratic form on the sign cube by

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\widetilde{Q}(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{t})=\left(\sum_{i=1}^{5}s_{i}\right)\left(\sum_{j=1}^{5}t_{j}\right)-3\sum_{i=1}^{5}s_{i}t_{i}.
``` |  | (42) |

Equation ([6](#S2.E6 "In Strictness of the lower bound. ‣ 2.1.1 Why the correspondence holds ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"))
then gives
$`Q(\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b})=\widetilde{Q}(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{t})`$. The
coordinate change is an invertible affine map between the Boolean and
sign cubes. Substitution in either direction does not increase
polynomial degree, so threshold degree is unchanged; affine forms also
remain affine.

Let $`A`$ and $`B`$ be the numbers of negative entries in $`\mathbf{s}`$
and $`\mathbf{t}`$, and let $`C`$ count coordinates at which both are
negative. Direct substitution gives

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\widetilde{Q}(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{t})=10+4(-A-B+AB-3C)\equiv 2\pmod{4}.
``` |  | (43) |

Thus $`\widetilde{Q}`$ never vanishes, so the polynomial $`Q`$ in
Equation ([6](#S2.E6 "In Strictness of the lower bound. ‣ 2.1.1 Why the correspondence holds ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"))
is a strict degree-two sign representation of $`f_{10}`$. On the
two-dimensional face of the sign cube

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbf{s}=(r,1,1,-1,-1),\qquad\mathbf{t}=(w,1,-1,1,-1),\qquad r,w\in\{-1,+1\},
``` |  | (44) |

we have $`\widetilde{Q}(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{t})=-2rw`$. Under the inverse
coordinate change, this is a two-dimensional face of the original
Boolean cube whose sign pattern is XOR, so it cannot be sign-represented
by an affine function. Consequently, $`\deg_{\pm}(f_{10})=2`$.

It remains to rule out two heads. If two heads represented $`f_{10}`$,
Equation ([40](#A5.E40 "In E.3 Threshold-Degree Lower Bound ‣ Appendix E Proofs of the Main Results ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"))
would give a strict sign-representing polynomial

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
P=cD_{1}D_{2}+N_{1}D_{2}+N_{2}D_{1}=(cD_{1}+N_{1})D_{2}+N_{2}D_{1}.
``` |  | (45) |

Since $`N_{1},N_{2},D_{1},D_{2}`$ are affine, this is a sum of two
products of affine forms. Pull this polynomial back to the sign cube by
setting

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
P^{\pm}(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{t})=P\left(\frac{\mathbf{1}-\mathbf{s}}{2},\frac{\mathbf{1}-\mathbf{t}}{2}\right),
``` |  | (46) |

where $`\mathbf{1}`$ denotes the all-ones vector. Because the coordinate
change is affine, the regrouping retains the form

|     |                                |     |      |
|-----|--------------------------------|-----|------|
|     |
       ``` math
       P^{\pm}=L_{1}R_{1}+L_{2}R_{2},
       ```                             |     | (47) |

where all four factors are affine in $`(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{t})`$, and
$`P^{\pm}`$ has the sign pattern of $`\widetilde{Q}`$. For a function
$`g`$ on the two signed blocks, define its mixed antipodal difference

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Delta g(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{t})=g(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{t})-g(\mathbf{s},-\mathbf{t})-g(-\mathbf{s},\mathbf{t})+g(-\mathbf{s},-\mathbf{t}).
``` |  | (48) |

Writing an affine form as
$`L(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{t})=\ell_{0}+\mathbf{c}_{L}\cdot\mathbf{s}+\mathbf{d}_{L}\cdot\mathbf{t}`$
gives

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Delta(LR)(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{t})=4\bigl[(\mathbf{c}_{L}\cdot\mathbf{s})(\mathbf{d}_{R}\cdot\mathbf{t})+(\mathbf{c}_{R}\cdot\mathbf{s})(\mathbf{d}_{L}\cdot\mathbf{t})\bigr].
``` |  | (49) |

Each product $`L_{h}R_{h}`$ therefore contributes two outer products,
$`4\mathbf{c}_{L_{h}}\mathbf{d}_{R_{h}}^{\top}`$ and
$`4\mathbf{c}_{R_{h}}\mathbf{d}_{L_{h}}^{\top}`$, to the mixed
coefficient matrix. Each has rank at most one. Thus
$`\Delta P^{\pm}(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{t})=\mathbf{s}^{\top}K\mathbf{t}`$
for a matrix $`K`$ with $`\operatorname{rank}(K)\leq 4`$.

For $`j\in[5]`$, let $`\mathbf{z}^{(j)}`$ have entry $`-1`$ in
coordinate $`j`$ and $`+1`$ elsewhere.
Equation ([42](#A5.E42 "In E.4 Strict Separation from Threshold Degree ‣ Appendix E Proofs of the Main Results ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"))
gives

|     |                                                    |     |      |
|-----|----------------------------------------------------|-----|------|
|     |
       ``` math
       \widetilde{Q}(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{z}^{(j)})=6s_{j},
       ```                                                 |     | (50) |

and negating either whole block reverses its sign. Set
$`Z=[\mathbf{z}^{(1)}\ \cdots\ \mathbf{z}^{(5)}]`$ and $`M=KZ`$. The
$`j`$th column of $`M`$ is the coefficient vector of the slice
$`\Delta P^{\pm}(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{z}^{(j)})=\sum_{i}M_{ij}s_{i}`$, and
$`\operatorname{rank}(M)\leq\operatorname{rank}(K)\leq 4`$. Since
$`P^{\pm}`$ has the sign pattern of $`\widetilde{Q}`$, all four terms in
this difference have sign $`s_{j}`$, giving

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
s_{j}\sum_{i}M_{ij}s_{i}>0\qquad\text{for every }\mathbf{s}\in\{-1,+1\}^{5}.
``` |  | (51) |

Fixing $`s_{j}=1`$ and choosing every other sign to oppose $`M_{ij}`$
yields

|     |                                |     |      |
|-----|--------------------------------|-----|------|
|     |
       ``` math
       M_{jj}>\sum_{i\neq j}|M_{ij}|.
       ```                             |     | (52) |

Thus $`M`$ is strictly column diagonally dominant and therefore
invertible, so it has rank five. This contradicts the bound
$`\operatorname{rank}(M)\leq 4`$ established above. Two heads cannot
represent $`f_{10}`$, proving $`3\leq H^{\ast}(f_{10})`$ and completing
Theorem [3](#Thmtheorem3 "Theorem 3 (Strict separation from threshold degree). ‣ Strictness of the lower bound. ‣ 2.1.1 Why the correspondence holds ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention").

### E.5 Weighted-Sum Interpolation

We prove
Theorem [4](#Thmtheorem4 "Theorem 4 (Weighted-sum interpolation). ‣ Constructive upper bounds. ‣ 2.1.1 Why the correspondence holds ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention").
Set $`M=|\operatorname{Im}(t_{\lambda})|`$. The claim is immediate when
$`M=1`$, so assume $`M\geq 2`$. Let $`\Lambda=\sum_{i}\lambda_{i}`$ and
enumerate the image of $`t_{\lambda}`$ as
$`0=\tau_{0}<\tau_{1}<\cdots<\tau_{M-1}`$.

Choose distinct $`\alpha_{1},\ldots,\alpha_{M-1}>1`$ and define

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\phi_{j}(\mathbf{x})=\frac{\alpha_{j}t_{\lambda}(\mathbf{x})}{1+\Lambda+(\alpha_{j}-1)t_{\lambda}(\mathbf{x})}=g_{j}(t_{\lambda}(\mathbf{x})).
``` |  | (53) |

The denominator is strictly positive on the cube and has strictly
positive slopes $`(\alpha_{j}-1)\lambda_{i}`$. Thus these affine ratios
are atoms by the coefficient characterization in
Appendix [E.1](#A5.SS1 "E.1 Linear-Fractional Normal Form ‣ Appendix E Proofs of the Main Results ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention").

It remains to show that $`1,g_{1},\ldots,g_{M-1}`$ form a basis for
functions on $`\operatorname{Im}(t_{\lambda})`$. Suppose a linear
combination of these functions vanishes on the image. Evaluation at
$`\tau_{0}=0`$ eliminates its constant coefficient. Dividing the
remaining equations by each $`\tau_{m}>0`$ and setting
$`r_{j}=(1+\Lambda)/(\alpha_{j}-1)`$ reduces them to
$`\sum_{j}d_{j}/(\tau_{m}+r_{j})=0`$ for $`m=1,\ldots,M-1`$. After
multiplication by $`\prod_{j}(s+r_{j})`$, the corresponding rational
function has a numerator of degree at most $`M-2`$ with $`M-1`$ distinct
roots. It is therefore identically zero. Evaluating at each pole
$`-r_{j}`$ shows that every $`d_{j}`$, and hence every original
coefficient, vanishes. The $`M`$ functions are linearly independent on
an $`M`$-point set, so they form a basis.

Interpolating the target signs gives a score
$`c+\sum_{j=1}^{M-1}a_{j}g_{j}(t_{\lambda}(\mathbf{x}))`$. Each scaled
term is an atom: multiplying its numerator by $`a_{j}`$ preserves
admissibility because its denominator has strictly positive slopes. The
normal form in
Theorem [1](#Thmtheorem1 "Theorem 1 (Linear-fractional normal form). ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention")
therefore gives an $`(M-1)`$-head representation. Taking
$`\lambda_{i}=2^{i-1}`$ makes $`t_{\lambda}`$ injective on the Boolean
cube, so $`M=2^{n}`$ and $`H^{\ast}(f)\leq 2^{n}-1`$ for every Boolean
function.

### E.6 Exact Symmetric Characterization

We prove
Theorem [5](#Thmtheorem5 "Theorem 5 (Exact symmetric characterization). ‣ 2.2 Exact Head Complexity for Symmetric Functions ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention").
Write $`\sigma_{k}=+1`$ when $`F(k)=1`$ and $`\sigma_{k}=-1`$ otherwise,
and let

|     |                                                          |     |      |
|-----|----------------------------------------------------------|-----|------|
|     |
       ``` math
       T=\{k\in[n]:\sigma_{k-1}\neq\sigma_{k}\},\qquad|T|=C(F).
       ```                                                       |     | (54) |

The polynomial

|     |                                                           |     |      |
|-----|-----------------------------------------------------------|-----|------|
|     |
       ``` math
       P(z)=\sigma_{0}\prod_{k\in T}\left(k-\frac{1}{2}-z\right)
       ```                                                        |     | (55) |

has sign $`\sigma_{k}`$ at every integer $`k\in\{0,\ldots,n\}`$ and
degree $`C(F)`$. Thus $`P(|\mathbf{x}|)`$ sign-represents $`f`$.

For the reverse threshold-degree inequality, take any degree-$`d`$
polynomial sign-representing $`f`$, multilinearize it on the Boolean
cube, and average it over all coordinate permutations. The averaged
polynomial remains a strict sign representation because $`f`$ is
symmetric. Every symmetric multilinear polynomial of degree at most
$`d`$, evaluated on a Boolean input of weight $`k`$, is a univariate
polynomial $`R(k)`$ of degree at most $`d`$: the degree-$`m`$ elementary
symmetric polynomial evaluates to $`\binom{k}{m}`$. Whenever $`F`$
changes between $`k-1`$ and $`k`$, the values $`R(k-1)`$ and $`R(k)`$
have opposite signs, so $`R`$ has a root in $`(k-1,k)`$. These intervals
are disjoint, giving $`d\geq C(F)`$. Hence

|     |                     |     |      |
|-----|---------------------|-----|------|
|     |
       ``` math
       \deg_{\pm}(f)=C(F),
       ```                  |     | (56) |

and
Theorem [2](#Thmtheorem2 "Theorem 2 (Threshold-degree lower bound). ‣ Unnormalized attention weights (denominator). ‣ 2.1.1 Why the correspondence holds ‣ 2.1 Characterizing Head Complexity ‣ 2 Autonomous Research Result ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention")
gives $`H^{\ast}(f)\geq C(F)`$.

For the upper bound, assume $`C=C(F)>0`$ and choose distinct
$`r_{1},\ldots,r_{C}>0`$. Set $`B(z)=\prod_{h=1}^{C}(z+r_{h})`$. Since
$`B(k)>0`$ at every Hamming weight, $`P/B`$ has the target sign pattern.
Partial fractions give

|     |                                                          |     |      |
|-----|----------------------------------------------------------|-----|------|
|     |
       ``` math
       \frac{P(z)}{B(z)}=c+\sum_{h=1}^{C}\frac{d_{h}}{z+r_{h}}.
       ```                                                       |     | (57) |

Each shifted reciprocal $`d_{h}/(|\mathbf{x}|+r_{h})`$ is an atom by
Appendix [E.1](#A5.SS1 "E.1 Linear-Fractional Normal Form ‣ Appendix E Proofs of the Main Results ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"):
its denominator is strictly positive on the cube and has all slopes
equal to one, while its numerator is constant.
Equation ([57](#A5.E57 "In E.6 Exact Symmetric Characterization ‣ Appendix E Proofs of the Main Results ‣ Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention"))
is therefore realized with $`C`$ heads. If $`C=0`$, $`f`$ is constant
and needs no heads. This proves $`H^{\ast}(f)\leq C(F)`$ and completes
the equality.
````
